t: LeetCode 1617 — Count Subtrees With Max Distance Between Cities
o: Every subset of cities that remains connected using only paths through the subset is a subtree, and we must tally, for each d = 1..n-1, how many subtrees have diameter exactly d (diameter = longest edge-count distance between two members). In Example 1 the three two-city subsets give d = 1, while four larger subsets reach d = 2 and none reaches 3. With n ≤ 15 there are at most 2^15 - 1 = 32767 nonempty subsets, so exhaustive bitmask enumeration is clearly intended. Per subset we need two facts: connectivity, and its diameter; single-city subsets are excluded because a diameter requires two distinct cities.
k: Tiny n (≤ 15) makes bitmask enumeration of all 2^n city subsets the intended framework.
A subset of a tree is connected iff the number of original edges with both endpoints inside equals |subset| - 1.
In a tree, the diameter of a connected subset equals the eccentricity of the farthest node from any member — hence double BFS.

a.i: Iterate every mask with at least two cities. A BFS restricted to mask cities from an arbitrary member reveals both connectivity (all popcount(mask) cities visited) and the farthest city; a second BFS from that farthest city returns the true diameter, a standard property of trees. Bucket the result into ans[diameter - 1].
s: For each mask with popcount ≥ 2, BFS from its lowest set bit visiting only mask cities.
If the visited count differs from popcount(mask), skip (disconnected).
Second BFS from the farthest city; its maximum distance is the diameter.
a.t: O(2ⁿ · n) — each of the 2ⁿ masks triggers two O(n) BFS traversals.
a.sp: O(n) — adjacency lists plus BFS buffers.

a.i: Run Floyd-Warshall once so dist[u][v] is available in O(1). For a connected mask, the diameter is simply the maximum pairwise distance among member cities — valid in trees because unique paths never leave a connected induced subset. Connectivity still uses the internal-edge-count criterion. This trades per-mask traversal logic for a plain double loop over pairs.
s: Compute all-pairs distances via Floyd-Warshall (or BFS from every node).
For each mask of size ≥ 2, count edges with both endpoints inside; require count == size - 1.
Otherwise take diameter = max dist[u][v] over mask pairs u < v.
a.t: O(n³ + 2ⁿ · n²) — Floyd-Warshall precompute plus up to n² pair checks per mask.

w:
## Wrap-up

Lead with bitmask + double BFS; offer the all-pairs variant as a cleanliness trade-off (simpler inner logic, slightly worse asymptotics). **Pitfalls:** treating one-city subsets as valid (they are never counted); calling the first BFS's maximum the diameter — wrong on star-shaped subsets, which is why double BFS is required; mixing 1-indexed city labels with 0-indexed bits.

**Edge cases:** n = 2 returns [1]; a path graph spreads counts across many diameters while a star concentrates them at 1. **Follow-ups:** for n up to ~100 the enumeration dies; switch to a tree DP over children tracking depth profiles and diameter histograms per node. Also try reporting only the number of connected (non-empty) subtrees regardless of diameter — a warm-up variant of the same masks.
